doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Founding the South Florida Jazz and Swing society
summary: He explains how the record club became a jazz society with 580 members, where he books and is artistic director.

venues.name: South Florida Jazz and Swing Society

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Okay. Good answer. I understand that you’re getting into the school system down where you live and talk about jazz a little bit?

Yeah, let me give you a little background. About a year or so ago I started getting calls for these gigs by this small organization called the South Florida Jazz and Swing Society, based in Delray Beach, which is just north of Boca Raton where I live. Now there’s a whole bunch of retired people, if you look at that area demographically, there’s a whole bunch of older folks, so you’d think that the swing/jazz demographic would be there. Sure enough, it is. There is an AM radio station there that plays swing and big band hits, and Scott Hamilton and Tony Bennett and Rosemary Clooney and that kind of stuff. So anyway, this thing started out as a record club. These guys would meet as record collectors and play records for each other and I understand it was twelve guys and then it was fifteen guys, and then it was eight guys, and then it was four guys, and then the last few months it was three guys, and one of the guys out of the three guys said this isn’t working, let’s change our operating basis here and let’s start having some live performances. So they did, and they organized themself up to the best of their ability which I hate to say now, in retrospect, wasn’t much because they didn’t know they were a corporation, they didn’t know they had to pay taxes. Of course now that we are an organization, largely because of the efforts of myself and my wife and our one friend Kurt Stern who’s been instrumental in organizing all this, with of course the help of all these volunteers, we now have a jazz society, the South Florida Jazz and Swing, based in Delray Beach/Boca, Boca/Delray, the Boca Raton, Delray Beach area, that boasts of 580 members and those are couples. Each membership is for two people so you do the math, and it was probably 50 people last year at this time, or 12-13 months ago it was probably 40 or 50 people. And my wife and I, she’s doing the administration, I’m doing the booking, and I’m artistic director and I’m the program committee and all this kind of stuff. So it’s been an interesting experience for me to be on a board of directors and booking things for an organization, and playing with many of them but not all of them, and we do ten concerts a year and so far we’ve had people like Tommy Flanagan, Allen Vache, Johnny Varro’s coming next month, we’re getting Dick Hyman, we had Paul Cohen’s big band, Paul Cohen is a lead trumpet player that used to play with Basie, Dorsey, Shaw, you name it. Etcetera, etcetera.
I think the artists probably like having a musician in the role of doing some of the booking you know.
The artists that you bring in. It probably makes it go pretty good. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -20-
